# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P0](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a fat, heavy-set woman who weighs two hundred pounds and is known to waddle when she walks. She keeps a sharp, all-seeing eye on everything that passes by her home.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c38 P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel is a capable, notable housewife who manages her own affairs and closely observes those of her neighbors. Extremely curious, opinionated, and outspoken, she prides herself on speaking her mind without hesitation and offering unsolicited advice. She is highly active in community and church organizations, and despite a pessimistic, pessimistic-sounding honesty, she possesses a kindly heart.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P21](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0021), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P30](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0030), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c15 P88](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0088), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road of Avonlea, where she kept watch over all travelers entering or leaving town. Upon learning that Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert planned to adopt an orphan boy, she immediately visited Green Gables to investigate and express her disapproval of the risky venture. Two weeks after Anne Shirley's arrival, Mrs. Rachel visited Green Gables after recovering from a bout of grippe and insulted Anne's looks, prompting Anne to fly into an intense temper. The following evening, Anne made a dramatic apology to Mrs. Rachel, who readily accepted it and allowed Anne to gather lilies from her garden. Mrs. Rachel frequently gave Marilla advice on raising Anne and managing school issues, such as suggesting leniency during Anne's feud with Mr. Phillips. When Matthew sought help securing a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Anne for Christmas, Mrs. Rachel made it for him.

## Quotes

> What on earth put such a notion into your head?  <sub>[v1 c1 P21](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0021)</sub>

> Well, I hope it will turn out all right. Only don’t say I didn’t warn you if he burns Green Gables down or puts strychnine in the well—I heard of a case over in New Brunswick where an orphan asylum child did that and the whole family died in fearful agonies. Only, it was a girl in that instance.  <sub>[v1 c1 P28](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0028)</sub>

> She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let move have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say.  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

> I did make a mistake in judging Anne, but it weren’t no wonder, for an odder, unexpecteder witch of a child there never was in this world, that’s what.  <sub>[v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)</sub>

> I declare I’m getting glad to sit down. I’ve been on my feet all day, and two hundred pounds is a good bit for two feet to carry round. It’s a great blessing not to be fat, Marilla. I hope you appreciate it. Well, Anne, I hear you’ve given up your notion of going to college. I was real glad to hear it. You’ve got as much education now as a woman can be comfortable with. I don’t believe in girls going to college with the men and cramming their heads full of Latin and Greek and all that nonsense.  <sub>[v1 c38 P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)</sub>
